title.en: I Can't Climb Trees Anymore (Ruskin Bond)

text.en: A grown man stands at a garden wall looking at the house where he spent his boyhood.

A visitor comes back to the old granite house of his childhood and sees the jackfruit tree still standing. A girl of twelve or thirteen speaks to him from the other side of the wall. As they talk, he remembers his grandmother's saying that a blessing rests on a house where a tree's shadow falls, and thinks of the treasures he once left there.
The story is about memory, the passing of time and the friendship that can grow between a young girl and an older man. The title tells us that the man who once climbed trees easily now finds that his age stops him, though his love for the tree has not changed.
Learn the shortened forms in the exercise (I'd, he's, wasn't, won't) and the vocabulary words drenched, dizzy, flourishing and prosperous. The writer paints a peaceful scene with careful details such as hollyhocks, the turnstile and the jackfruit tree.
